name: quantitative-audit-cases

labelling.labeller: Claude (the same agent that writes the auditor's rules)
labelling.status: author-labelled; NOT an independent measurement and not the M3 result. Precision/recall on this set are provisional until an independent labeller reviews or relabels it.

label_guide.rule: Label what a careful human reader can conclude from the two texts alone (plus the case's entities), NOT what the auditor's regexes can detect. When several categories apply, the first in this order wins: unit_or_denominator_difference, baseline_or_period_difference, method_or_scope_difference, consistent_within_rounding_or_uncertainty, same_metric_value_disagreement, unresolved_discrepancy.
label_guide.unit_or_denominator_difference: Values are not comparable because units or denominators differ (incl. % vs percentage points, bits vs bytes, per day vs per week, per capita vs total).
label_guide.baseline_or_period_difference: A period or a baseline/reference is stated on both sides and differs (incl. relative vs absolute risk, placebo vs baseline comparisons).
label_guide.method_or_scope_difference: A method (mean/median, nominal/real, market/book, exchange rate/PPP), geography, population, product/entity, setting or endpoint is stated on both sides and differs.
label_guide.consistent_within_rounding_or_uncertaint: Values agree within stated precision, a stated range or interval, an approximation, or an equivalent restatement.
label_guide.same_metric_value_disagreement: The texts report the same metric for the same scope, period and method, and the values are incompatible beyond rounding or stated uncertainty.
label_guide.unresolved_discrepancy: The texts do not contain enough information to decide whether a difference is real.

split.method: within each label, cases ordered by sha256(seed:case_id); first floor(n/2) -> tuning, rest -> held_out
